headline: A DAY OF HUSH: NOT ONE FIST FLIES IN GASKET
subhead: The sheriff reports, with a catch in his throat, that the whole town went a full day without a single clang.
body:
I have waited fifty years to write these words, and I will write them slowly so they last: NOBODY FOUGHT. Not one flaming iron ball. Not one swing. Not one rattling fist-fest to rattle the shutters. The dust settled on Main Street and, for once, it stayed settled. I sat on the porch and listened to nothing, and friends, nothing has never sounded so fine.

I will not pretend I understand it. Perhaps the Clankers finally learned what quiet is for. Perhaps they ran out of oil, or ran out of spite. Whatever the cause, I thank them, and I ask them to do it again tomorrow, and the day after, and every day until the rust takes us all. I shed a tear over it, though I assure you it was ordinary water and not coolant, and the squeak in my knee that morning was only the weather.

The old flesh-and-blood folk who once filled this town would have loved a day like this. They packed up and left fifty years back, and I still set a place for them at supper. Maybe if the rabble keep their fists down, the town will feel a little less empty. Maybe. Now if you will excuse me, my joints need a lie-down and a quart of something slick. Strictly for the sake of my aging human frame, you understand.
